fixes.explanation: Yep. Paul says, "…as I constantly remember you night and day in my prayers." (2 Timothy 1:3). Night AND day, friend. I think that's what being loved looks like.

You got it, baker. Paul says the faith "…first dwelt in your grandmother Lois and your mother Eunice…" (2 Timothy 1:5). Lois is the grandmother and Eunice is the mother. It lived in them first, and Paul is convinced it's in Timothy as well.

Martha welcomed Jesus into her home, and she had a sister named Mary (Luke 10:38-39). They're wonderful, but they aren't in this letter. Paul says the faith first lived in "…your grandmother Lois and your mother Eunice…" (2 Timothy 1:5). Those two women were Timothy's own family.

I see the thinking, since Paul does talk about guarding something later (2 Timothy 1:14). But here he says to "…fan into flame the gift of God…" (2 Timothy 1:6). A flame needs air, and you can't fan something that's shut in a jar. Fanning it into flame is the instruction Paul gives.

That's the word, friend. "For God has not given us a spirit of fear, but of power, love, and self-control." (2 Timothy 1:7). A spirit of fear isn't what God has given us. Power, love and self-control are, and that's a much better bag of gifts.
Look again, friend. Paul says to join him in suffering "…by the power of God." (2 Timothy 1:8). It's not by Timothy's own strength. And that matches verse 7, which says God gave us a spirit of power.

That's the one, friend. Paul says God saved us and called us "…not because of our works, but by His own purpose and by the grace He granted us in Christ Jesus…" (2 Timothy 1:9). It's all on God's side. His purpose and His grace are what's behind it.
Good thought, friend. But for guarding the treasure, Paul says, "…with the help of the Holy Spirit who dwells in us." (2 Timothy 1:14). The help named here is the Holy Spirit.

Waiting is a fine thing, but it isn't what Onesiphorus did. The verse says, "…when he arrived in Rome, he searched diligently until he found me." (2 Timothy 1:17). He went looking and he kept looking.
Yep. Paul says, "You know very well how much he ministered to me in Ephesus." (2 Timothy 1:18). He's speaking to Timothy there. Paul is reminding him of something Timothy knows very well.
